issues.title: PM6 amended Stage 2A/2B: synthesis dependencies and BRS2(KC1) reassessed
issues.public_title: Acetylcholine synthesis inputs and shared one-carbon constraint corrected
issues.public_description: Acetylcholine synthesis uses choline and acetyl-CoA after choline enters cholinergic nerve endings. Phosphatidylcholine can provide choline, and vitamin B5 supports the coenzyme A route to acetyl-CoA. One-carbon impairment can constrain the shared choline resource, but extra intake has not been shown here to raise human brain acetylcholine.
issues.public_decision: Keep choline as the Direct substrate, list phosphatidylcholine as its Derived provision route, list acetyl-CoA and its vitamin B5 precursor in the biochemical inventory, and map BRS2(KC1) without copying its nutrient or food list.
public_findings: Choline transport and the choline-acetyl-CoA reaction are the defining synthesis steps.
Phosphatidylcholine provides choline; vitamin B5 supports acetyl-CoA provision through coenzyme A.
Animal models support a constrained relationship between one-carbon status and the brain choline-acetylcholine resource.
findings: The prior rerun omitted high-affinity choline transport and did not adjudicate the acetyl-CoA/pantothenate provision chain.
The amended follow-up separates blood-brain choline delivery from terminal CHT uptake and covers compartmented cytosolic acetyl-CoA supply.
Thiamine was screened but not admitted: the available severe-deficiency study changed acetyl-CoA distribution and acetylcholine release, not ChAT activity or measured synthesis flux.
Acetyl-CoA is admitted as a biochemical substrate; phosphatidylcholine is a Derived choline-provision route and vitamin B5 is a biochemical cofactor precursor.
B12, folate and betaine remain outside the PM dietary inventory because they are not ChAT substrates or cofactors.
BRS2(KC1) is established as constrained-by through a cited mechanistic chain; its constituents and foods are not inherited.

issues.title: Broccoli sprout homogenate is a food preparation, not a supplement
issues.public_title: Broccoli sprout homogenate is a food preparation
issues.public_description: The admitted practice is a three-day broccoli sprout homogenate prepared with added myrosinase. It is not an ordinary broccoli serving and not a sulforaphane capsule.
issues.public_decision: Admit the homogenate under Food Preparation and Delivery. Do not admit a sulforaphane supplement.
public_findings: Riedl 2009 gave healthy adults a broccoli sprout homogenate once a day for three days. The sprouts were blended with water, mixed with daikon sprouts, and held at 37°C so myrosinase could finish forming sulforaphane.
Nasal-cell RNA for phase II enzymes rose. Alfalfa sprout homogenate did not. Nrf2 protein and brain endpoints were not measured.
Wise 2016 gave people with COPD capsules of sulforaphane extracted from broccoli sprouts for four weeks. Lung Nrf2 target-gene expression did not rise.
findings: The previous conditional-supplementation entry blended the homogenate, isolated oral doses, and sulforaphane-yielding supplements.
Houghton cites the Riedl homogenate for the airway gene result and only calculates that a myrosinase-active powder might match that dose.
The Wise capsule trial is a null on lung target-gene expression. It does not erase the homogenate result, and the homogenate result does not erase the null.
issues.decision: Replace PM3-SOP-1 with the myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate under food_prep. Do not admit a supplement.
issues.rationale: Source check of the methods, not expert review. The tested food formulation is the homogenate. The tested capsule formulation did not raise the lung gene endpoint.
issues.required_action: Do not restore oral broccoli-derived sulforaphane as a supplement, and do not turn the three-day homogenate into an ordinary crucifer pattern.

issues.title: Vitamin C does not constrain Nrf2 activation on this page
issues.public_title: Vitamin C is not a constraint on this activation step
issues.public_description: Vitamin C stays a direct antioxidant in the sources. It is not shown to constrain Nrf2 activation. Zinc and selenium are cofactors of downstream enzymes, not of the switch.
issues.public_decision: Remove the vitamin C key-constraint disclosure. Do not admit zinc or selenium as requirements of Nrf2 activation.
public_findings: Verlaet lists vitamin C as a water-soluble non-enzymatic antioxidant.
Houghton reports ascorbic acid as a much weaker NQO1 inducer than sulforaphane, and treats ascorbate as a direct antioxidant used up in the reaction.
Verlaet places zinc on copper-zinc superoxide dismutase and selenium on glutathione peroxidase.
findings: General antioxidant relevance is not evidence that vitamin C availability constrains this activation step.
The 2019 zinc and selenium chapter was not retrieved in full, so it is not used as a new admission.
issues.decision: Withdraw the vitamin C KC disclosure. Leave zinc and selenium out of cofactors and dietary requirements.
issues.rationale: Source check, not expert review. Empty requirement fields remain appropriate. They do not block the food-preparation practice.
issues.required_action: Do not restore vitamin C as a constraint on this activation step unless a source shows that its availability limits the switch.

issues.title: Diet-Dominant and the repeated-exposure claim are not supported
issues.public_title: Diet is not established as the principal route

issues.public_decision: Use Diet-Supported. Place the admitted food-preparation practice at 1.1, because no direct dietary requirement is established. Remove the repeated-exposure claim.
public_findings: Houghton says phase II enzymes can last for days, so induction need not be continuous. It does not compare repeated exposure with a single dose.
The only admitted intervention effect is the three-day homogenate. Absence of another admitted route does not establish dietary dominance.
findings: The previous Overview and finding said repeated exposure was more meaningful than a single dose. That sentence is not in Houghton.
The dominance contract requires a separate principal-route decision. A dietary inducer alone does not establish it.
issues.decision: Set intervention dominance to Diet-Supported. Place the admitted food-preparation practice at 1.1 because no direct dietary requirement is established.
issues.rationale: Source check, not expert review. Diet-Supported is kept. The homogenate is the only admitted lever, so it occupies section 1.1. That placement does not make diet dominant.
issues.required_action: Do not restore Diet-Dominant or the repeated-exposure sentence without a source that compares repeated and single exposure.

issues.title: Therapeutic Area (ADHD) evidence claims for cortisol records misstate direction and demonstration type
findings: EC000161 (Chang 2021) says "altered" basal and morning cortisol; the source finding is specifically lower morning cortisol with no afternoon difference (Pilot 1 defect 1).
EC000162 (Chang 2020) and EC000164 (Lane 2010) are coded demonstration: symptom-improvement; both are cross-sectional case-control studies with no intervention.
EC000164 lists Lane 2010 as supportive for PM4 cortisol; its cortisol results were null and its only significant result was electrodermal (PM6 biology).
The records project onto BRS6-FM2-PM4, BRS6-FM3-PM6 and BRS6-FM4-PM9 via the Therapeutic Area evidence section, sourced from the BRS6 hub page.
issues.required_action: Re-adjudicate EC000161-EC000164 against the PM4-F7 synthesis and Pilot 1 record: preserve direction (lower), recode demonstration as association, and route Lane 2010 to PM6. Do not edit study facts on PM pages.
